title: The Portrait of Marrow Creek
premise: Pest controller Ivo Lockridge is hired by the ailing Vess family of Marrow Creek to deal with something in the walls that leaves small, human fingerprints. When their sleep-recording app captures a second voice answering questions no one asked aloud, Ivo realizes the house is counting its inhabitants — and the count must always come out even. As Ivo grows bonded to the Vess family, they discover the 'pest' is the unclaimed heir of a century-old inheritance, kept in the dry well beneath the house, and that the family patriarch intends to refill the well with a replacement. In the end, Ivo chooses found family over contract, empties the well by naming the heir aloud, and walks out with the surviving Vesses as the count finally closes at zero.
about_author: Zephyrine Marchetti is the pen name of a former rural building inspector who spent a decade documenting the strange maintenance requests of old farmhouses. They write horror about houses that remember their tenants, and live, carefully, in a home with no basement.

chapters.title: The Callout Fee
chapters.summary: Ivo Lockridge, a meticulous pest controller who counts doors and keeps lights burning, takes an unusually lucrative job at the Vess farmhouse in Marrow Creek. Told from Ivo's POV. The beat is wary professionalism: something in the walls leaves fingerprints too small and too human to file under 'rodent.'

chapters.title: Small Hands, Old Plaster
chapters.summary: Ivo finds handprints behind the plaster, arranged in a descending line toward the cellar. Patriarch Aldous Vess deflects every question while his grandchildren, Wren and Tam, quietly befriend the outsider. Ivo's POV. Emotional beat: the first pull of belonging against professional detachment.

chapters.title: Questions at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Wren shows Ivo the family's sleep recordings: every night, a second voice answers questions the sleeping family never asked. Ivo listens to their own recording and hears the voice say their name. Ivo's POV. Beat: dread curdling into compulsion — the house has begun counting them.

chapters.title: The Even Count
chapters.summary: Ivo maps the house and realizes the fingerprints always appear in pairs; when one vanishes, another appears. Tam goes briefly 'missing' and returns wrong-eyed, insisting he never left. Alternating Ivo and Wren POV. Beat: the horror is arithmetic, and the family is one body short of even.

chapters.title: What Aldous Signed
chapters.summary: Ivo finds a deed from 1897 in the attic: the Vess inheritance requires a 'kept heir' in the dry well, renewed each generation. Aldous, dying, has arranged a refill. Wren's POV. Beat: betrayal — the grandfather they nursed has been pricing his grandchildren.

chapters.title: The Well Breathes
chapters.summary: The well beneath the kitchen refills with something like water, something like voices. The second voice on the recordings grows clearer: it is the kept heir, asking to be named. Ivo's POV, drawn literally into the cellar dark. Beat: Ivo crosses from observer to participant, pulled 'straight into the middle of it.'

chapters.title: Kinship Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Wren and Ivo research the original heir, a disowned Vess child erased from the family Bible. Naming her would empty the well — but Aldous has locked the parish records and begun moving the family toward the cellar door. Wren's POV. Beat: found family hardening into a plan.

chapters.title: The Night of Refilling
chapters.summary: Aldous drugs the household and begins the rite; Tam, still half-wrong, nearly leads Wren down. Ivo wakes, keeps the lights on, and fights the house's doors, which now count themselves shut. Ivo's POV. Beat: terror and resolve — one person against an inheritance with a schedule.

chapters.title: A Name Spoken Downward
chapters.summary: At the well's rim, Ivo speaks the erased heir's name — Mercy Vess — into the rising dark, and the well answers by giving the voice a face and letting it climb out. Aldous is taken by the count instead, the arithmetic closing on him. Ivo and Wren POV interwoven. Beat: climax, sacrifice, and the count breaking.

chapters.title: Zero, and Morning
chapters.summary: The farmhouse stands quiet; the fingerprints fade, the recordings fall silent. Mercy, freed, chooses to leave rather than haunt, and Ivo — offered payment and offered family, takes only the family — drives out with Wren and Tam. Ivo's POV. Beat: resolution, grief for Aldous, and the fragile warmth of a family that chose itself.
